purpose: Test the over-strong relation bias hypothesis using observed logit scales, actual attention changes, and checkpoint-internal inference sensitivity.

figures.stage4ad_logit_scale_by_target: Compare mean absolute formal base logits and relation biases across target types; scale alone does not establish harm.
figures.stage4ad_bias_base_ratio_heatmap: Compare ratios of pooled absolute means across nine directed target-source pairs.
figures.stage4ad_attention_entropy_shift: Show the signed entropy change on real incoming neighborhoods; concentration has no inherent quality interpretation.
figures.stage4ad_top_neighbor_switch: Compare actual neighbor identity switching across target types independently from entropy.
figures.stage4ad_lambda_sensitivity: Show all five prescribed inference scales without smoothing or selecting a new model.
figures.stage4ad_lambda_motion_sensitivity: Show the same five scales on frozen displacement-defined motion groups.

statistics: Population means on all actual VAL edge-layer-head or target-layer-head observations; no independent-sample confidence intervals.
review_risks: Overlapping actor windows and attention heads are not independent replicates.
Absolute logit offsets can cancel in softmax; ratio is only a scale diagnostic.
Target edge weighting differs from target-node weighting; both are explicit in source tables.
Directed pair entropy contexts overlap and use the whole original neighborhood.
Lambda=0 retains Stage4A trained shared weights and is not Stage3B.
Lambda sensitivity does not replace the formal lambda=1 NOT SUPPORTED conclusion.
Small sensitivity differences require readable numeric source tables and unambiguous axes.
